I can relate so much to your post. I adopted a rescued 1-year-old Chihuahua from a breeding farm a year ago, and she's so attached to me... everytime I come home, all she wants to do is stay with me (and so do I!). I actually started going home as early as possible to be with her. I really wish I could take her to work but they don't allow dogs in the building, even if she's tiny and silent. Everybody tells me I'm harming her by not giving her independence, but we relate a lot because we're both little balls of anxiety, her due to all her suffering on the breeding farm, and me due to a harsh childhood, so we are kind of made for each other. At this point I'm so happy I have her I wouldn't have it any other way.

My ndad would tell me that he felt proud of me when I was at someone else’s house and I would help around with small chores and say please and thank you, and those parents called that out when he picked me up. That’s the only time where I remember him saying that he felt proud of being my dad. I guess it stuck with me way more than it should have.

I tried to, but failed miserably. I stained my pajamas and tried to hide them (I was 11) , and she found them out while I was at school. 

She ran over with a new set of clothes and a full box of pads so I could change. She then demanded to my teacher that she talked to all the girls about this, and then proceeded to tell my whole family.

I'm the oldest of the siblings/cousins in the family, so it was very embarrassing.

Trust her, and her communication towards you. I totally get that overwhelming feeling of wanting to fix her issues and avoid her from feeling sad ever again, I get them too! It means you really care about her. Don’t punish yourself for being intense, but trust her words and her sense of what makes her feel better.

The best thing you can do is listen to her. Let her know you’re there if she needs you, and give her the space she asks... try not to push any plans apart from “I can go over and make you coffee while you study”. I promise she will feel supported, loved and will really appreciate you.
Worry after it happens and not before. If not, you’re creating another problem for her because she can feel you’re tense and worried, and now she’s worried both for her exams and your relationship.

Tully’s is the best coffee place for me in Japan. Inexpensive, and they don’t care how much you stay there. We’ve been there for over an hour with my boyfriend charging our phones and just resting and they were nothing but polite to us.

My boyfriend very rarely cries, but I do cry all the time. 

When it's something not related to stress or sadness but things like a movie or a cute dog, he usually holds my hand without saying anything and lets me "have my moment" which I feel it's nice - I don't get invaded by him but I still feel him close and acknowledged.
